## Decisions made (and why)

**The pod "completion" race — fixed in THREE places, this is the big one.**
`sky360._run`, `process_backdrops.depth_via_comfy` and `neural_sr._run_pod` all submitted a
ComfyUI job then polled `/queue` until idle, then took `ls -t <tag>_*.png | head -1`. The
queue can read empty *before* ComfyUI registers a just-POSTed prompt, so the first poll
breaks immediately and `ls -t` copies the **previous run's output for that scene** — silently,
in ~1s, all the way through to a packed HEIC. Observed live on carina_mystic. All three now
snapshot the output listing *before* submitting and wait for a filename they have not seen.
`neural_sr` was the worst-placed because `sr_equirect` runs on every scene against tags that
accumulate files across every previous render. **If you add another pod stage, use this
pattern.** A ~1s stage time is the tell.

**`kind` is measured, but fov is a missing term in that rule.** `potm_auto_manifest.border_level`
(brightest of four edge medians) was applied to the 9 hand rows for the first time; four were
wrong. m31 (border 143) and ngc4631_whale (51) became `field` — that fixed the "images stacked
on top of each other" report at its root, since the object recipe had been painting a *second*
galaxy. But m8_lagoon (border 1.3) was moved to `object` and that made it **worse** — a circular
porthole. At fov 144 the footprint spans most of the forward view, so a hard-bounded fill reads
as a porthole rather than a hero in the void. It is back to `field`. The measurement is a good
proxy for narrow objects and a bad one at large fov.

**The object fill must have NO distance falloff.** This was my regression and it broke every
object scene (sombrero, m106, m8_lagoon, potm2508a → glowing portholes). A flat fill is uniform
over the whole sphere so there is no boundary for diffusion to find; dimming it toward a floor
creates a bounded disc of lighter sky that the outpaint develops into a rimmed halo. It was
added to stop m31 washing grey, but m31's real problem was being mis-typed. **Fields keep the
falloff — that is where it was needed and verified (potm2307a).**

**Do not change several things at once mid-render.** Two separate regressions this session came
from batching changes and then having to untangle which caused what.

**Blender earns its place only on Saturn's rings.** `CustomMaterial` is unavailable on visionOS
(Xcode rejects it in xrOS) — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` from Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written
Metal. So built-in shadows can't give the ring shadow band on the globe or the globe's shadow
across the rings. Plan: model in Blender, ray-trace in Cycles, **bake the shadowing into
textures**, export USDZ, load as real geometry in RealityKit. Bake the *lighting*, never the
*geometry* — stereo parallax must stay real. Frozen lighting is fine for a body that rotates
once per 10.6 h.

**Planets/moons go in as geometry, not baked into the equirect.** The backdrop sits at one
near-infinite depth (`depth_floor 0.94`, 0.22% baseline), so anything pasted there has no
parallax — a large part of why saturn1 reads as a picture.

**"Huge" and "sharp" trade against each other.** Filling more view means you're closer, seeing
less surface magnified more. Required cylindrical map width ≈ `360 × 34 px/deg × R/(d−R)`:
30°→4.3K, 40°→6.4K, 50°→9K, 60°→12.2K, 80°→22K, 90°→29.5K. Iapetus (11741 real) is crisp to
~59°; Venus (8192 real) to ~47°; Saturn/Jupiter are only 4096 *real* under an 8192 SR, so honest
detail runs out ~29°. **Saturn's escape:** the rings span ~2.3× the globe radius, so the ring
system can fill 80–90° while the globe subtends 35–40°.

**Starfield per scene = yaw-only rotation.** Baked stereo disparity is horizontal in equirect
space with a pole falloff; any pitch/roll tilts it off the interocular axis → vertical disparity
→ nauseating. Yaw alone gives plenty of variety. Measured on `deep_star_map`: forward-view
brightness swings 6× across yaw. Four well-separated angles: **165°** sparse (mean 0.31),
**0°** band high +12° (0.36), **105°** band level (0.93), **255°** dense galactic centre (1.91).
Use `deep_star_map` (real Gaia/Tycho, HDR EXR, already in pipeline), not the Solar System Scope
8k_stars — same 8192×4096 but an 8-bit artist JPEG.

**Splash freeze was never the animation's fault.** `SplashView` derives phase from
`context.date`, so a blocked main thread *freezes* it and then jumps. First fix attempt moved
only the file read off-main and did NOT work, because `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex` returns
a **lazy** CGImage — the decode deferred until `TextureResource` touched the pixels, back on
main. `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true` is what actually relocates the cost.

- **The composition survives as a still frame.** The three ripple rings are rendered frozen at phases 0.16 / 0.49 / 0.82 of the old expansion curve, so it keeps the layered-ripple silhouette rather than collapsing to a bare circle. Guide ring, mote, starfield, FLOAT, and tagline are unchanged.
- **The progress hairline is deleted, not frozen.** A stationary bar reads as a stalled bar — worse than nothing. The status line ("LOADING STARMAPS…") now carries that job alone, moved up to where the hairline sat.

Every value in that view was driven by the main run loop, so anything animated there freezes and jumps for exactly as long as the upload blocks. Confirming which RealityKit call it is would need Instruments on device, and it wouldn't change the outcome for the splash either way.

4	// §7b transition flash — a brief full-view fade that masks a scene change. Kept from the
5	// (now retired) generated L1–L4 pipeline because the spatial-image scene system still uses
6	// it to mask a jump/select between skies. Everything else that lived here — the generated
7	// far backdrop, L2 nebula (splat/particle), L3 star volume, L4 phenomena — was removed when
8	// the app moved to a pre-rendered stereo-image library (see SpatialImageEnvironment).
9	// Fades to BLACK, not white (device round 7). A white flash masks a change by
10	// saturating, but between two dark deep-space scenes it reads as a jolt — the eye is
11	// dark-adapted and gets slammed to full brightness and back. Black masks just as
12	// completely (alpha 1 fully occludes either way) and costs the viewer nothing.
13	// Type names still say "Whiteout" so this stays a one-file change; see FADE_TINT.
14	struct WhiteoutComponent: Component {
15	    var active = false
16	    var elapsed: TimeInterval = 0
17	    var fadeIn: TimeInterval = 0.25
18	    var hold: TimeInterval = 0.12
19	    var fadeOut: TimeInterval = 0.45
20	    var total: TimeInterval { fadeIn + hold + fadeOut }
21	}

23	/// 0 = black, 1 = white. One constant, used by both the per-frame tint and the initial
24	/// material, so they can never disagree.
25	let FADE_TINT: CGFloat = 0

27	struct WhiteoutSystem: System {
28	    static let query = EntityQuery(where: .has(WhiteoutComponent.self))
29	    init(scene: Scene) {}
30	    func update(context: SceneUpdateContext) {
31	        MainActor.assumeIsolated {
32	            for e in context.entities(matching: Self.query, updatingSystemWhen: .rendering) {
33	                guard var c = e.components[WhiteoutComponent.self], c.active,
34	                      let me = e as? ModelEntity else { continue }
35	                c.elapsed += context.deltaTime
36	                var a: Float
37	                if c.elapsed < c.fadeIn {
38	                    a = Float(c.elapsed / c.fadeIn)                                   // fade to black
39	                } else if c.elapsed < c.fadeIn + c.hold {
40	                    a = 1                                                            // peak (swap happens here)
41	                } else if c.elapsed < c.total {
42	                    a = Float(1 - (c.elapsed - c.fadeIn - c.hold) / c.fadeOut)         // reveal new env
43	                } else {
44	                    a = 0; c.active = false
45	                }
46	                a = max(0, min(1, a))

**BUILD SUCCEEDED.** (SourceKit's "cannot find in scope" spray is the usual noise — it lost the module index; the compiler resolves all of it.)

The diagnosis was a timing race, not a colour problem. `maskedSwap` slept a fixed 0.30 s, called the swap, and returned — but the swap only *started* an async decode taking seconds. The flash meanwhile ran its fixed 0.82 s course and faded out on schedule, uncovering the sphere that was still mounted (the old sky). Seconds later the decode landed and `attach` cut to the new sky with no mask left. Exactly the three beats you saw: black → original → jump.

The fix makes the mask outlast the work instead of guessing at its duration:

- **`WhiteoutComponent.holding`** (`Float/Layers/DepthLayers.swift`) — while set, the overlay parks at full black and its clock is clamped to the end of `hold`, so release always drops straight into the fade-out no matter how long the wait ran. `hold` is now a *minimum*, not the whole peak.
- **`maskedSwap(to:)`** (`Float/App/AppModel.swift`) — kicks off `prepare(index:)` at the same instant as the fade-in, awaits it, waits for the overlay to actually be opaque, attaches, then clears `holding`. The reveal is now driven by the load finishing.
- The opacity wait polls the component's own `elapsed` rather than sleeping 0.25 s of wall clock, since the flash advances on the render clock — that mismatch is what made the original fixed sleep fragile in the first place.
- A failed load (`prepare` returns nil) still releases, fading back to the current sky rather than parking at black.
- `selectScene` now checks "swap in flight" *before* writing `currentScene`/UserDefaults. The in-flight window is a full decode now, so a second tap during it would previously have persisted a sky that never loaded.

One consequence worth deciding on: a scene change now sits at full black for the entire decode — seconds, not 0.82 s. That's the honest cost; the old version only felt shorter because it showed you the wrong sky. If that hold turns out to feel too long in the headset, the lever is the same one behind the splash stutter — the decode itself — and options there are pre-decoding the *next* sky speculatively, or putting a status line on the black the way the splash now does.

Fix splash stutter, scene-swap race; sky recipe r10; pod completion race

App:
- SplashView is now static. Its ripple/mote/drift/sweep all derived phase from
  the TimelineView date, so the main-thread stall during scene load froze them
  and then jumped. Moving the 150 MP HEIC decode off-main (with
  kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately, which is what actually relocates a lazy
  CGImage's cost) removed one stall but not the stutter; the rest is RealityKit's
  texture upload and cannot be moved. Rings are frozen at spread phases so the
  composition survives. Status line "LOADING STARMAPS…" replaces the sweep bar.
- Scene transition held a fixed 0.82 s while the swap it was masking took
  seconds, so it faded to black, revealed the OLD sky, then cut to the new one
  unmasked. WhiteoutComponent.holding now parks the overlay at full black until
  the load actually lands. Decode starts with the fade-in rather than after it.
- Fade is to black, not white: between two dark scenes a white flash slams a
  dark-adapted eye, and alpha 1 occludes either way.
- Startup restructured: first sky decodes before the immersive space opens, so
  it never comes up as empty black limbo.
- recenter() — yaw-only (pitch/roll would tilt baked stereo disparity off the
  interocular axis), snaps rather than slews (vection), auto-runs at launch.

Pipeline:
- Pod completion race in sky360/process_backdrops/neural_sr: all three polled
  /queue until idle then took `ls -t | head -1`, but the queue can read empty
  before ComfyUI registers a just-POSTed prompt — silently copying the PREVIOUS
  run's output for that scene. All three now wait for an unseen filename.
- sky360 r10: edge-clamp fill replaces mirror-tiling, noise far-field seed
  (mirror-tiled detail carried p2p 80 vs 10 blurred — most of the ghosting),
  angular FAR_FALLOFF_DEG, superellipse footprint, object branch flat fill with
  no distance falloff (falloff creates the bounded disc that outpaints into a
  rimmed porthole; fields keep it).
- stereo_synth: sub-pixel forward warp. round() quantised disparity into 13
  integer terraces per hemisphere on every scene. Also fixes a pre-existing
  inverted z-priority where the right eye let the far surface win.
- master_sr: SR_BACKEND defaults to esrgan; USDU manufactured 3.6x the edge
  roughness of a plain resample. Adds --redo.
- scripts/rerender_all.py: resumable two-phase runner with progress/ETA.

Re-rendered assets are deliberately NOT in this commit — that render is still
running and the files are mid-flight.
